items.text: President [[p:Isaac Herzog]] gave [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]], leader of the centrist Yashar party, the first mandate to form Israel's next government after 67 of 120 incoming MKs recommended him, a setback for Prime Minister [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]]. Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by two weeks, and says an emergency coalition will need unconventional steps and compromise from all sides.
items.outlet: The Times of Israel; AP (via PBS)
items.notes: Election held 27 Oct. Bloc counts differ: AP gives Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48, Arab-led parties 19; ToI says 46 MKs back Netanyahu. Formal ceremony evening of 8 Nov. On 9 Nov Trump called the two men's policies very similar (ToI liveblog).

items.text: An explosive-laden drone hit the [[p:Dana Gas]]-operated Khor Mor gas facility in Sulaimani province late on 8 Nov, starting a fire and halting production. The [[p:Kurdistan Regional Government]] says 2,500–2,800 MW was lost, over 70% of the region's power. No one has claimed the attack; Baghdad ordered a joint investigation.
items.notes: No official attribution. Unofficial accounts cited by Kurdistan24 point to a launch near Tuz Khurmatu; claims of an Iranian strike are unsupported. Al Jazeera says any link to the US–Iran war is unclear. Same facility hit in Nov 2025. No casualties. No restart date from Dana Gas.

items.text: The COP31 climate conference opened in Antalya after a delay over whether climate finance would be on the agenda. Türkiye holds the presidency under [[p:Murat Kurum]], while Australia's [[p:Chris Bowen]] leads negotiations under a power-sharing deal. The Trump administration sent no officials, and few breakthroughs are expected amid an oil price shock.
items.notes: Runs 9–20 Nov; World Leaders' Summit 11–12 Nov. Türkiye is pushing a voluntary pledge to raise electricity's share of global energy use to 35% by 2035. TRT World is Turkish state media. Outlook ('few breakthroughs') is AFP's assessment.

items.text: The [[p:Electoral Commission of South Africa]] declared final local election results: the [[p:African National Congress]] came first with 30.76%, its worst result since 1994, ahead of the [[p:Democratic Alliance (South Africa)|Democratic Alliance]] (24.64%), the [[p:uMkhonto weSizwe Party|MK Party]] (9.76%) and the [[p:Economic Freedom Fighters|EFF]] (6.22%). Only 74 of 213 councils have a majority, so coalition talks begin, notably in the Gauteng metros.
items.notes: Borderline Tier 1 (pressure on the GNU partners). Hung-council counts conflict between outlets (127–142). Turnout 52%. ActionSA 5.67%. Ramaphosa urged good-faith coalition talks.
